comments: Hosmer-Lemeshow Calibration Test Suite
Self-contained tests for the Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit statistic,
used to assess calibration of logistic regression models.
The HL statistic partitions predictions into 10 decile bins and computes
a chi-squared statistic comparing observed vs. expected event counts.
Under good calibration HL ~ χ²(8) (8 df since outer cells are constrained).
Reference: Hosmer & Lemeshow, "Goodness-of-fit tests for the multiple
logistic regression model", Comm. Stat. Theory Methods (1980).
All functions inlined (tests cannot import stdlib).

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `rapamycin_epistemic_pbpk`. Rapamycin (Sirolimus) Epistemic PBPK Test Suite Validates GUM-based uncertainty propagation through a 3-compartment rapamycin model: Blood, Brain (BBB-limited), Peripheral (fast-eq. tissues). It should compile and run successfully.
description: Rapamycin (Sirolimus) Epistemic PBPK Test Suite Validates GUM-based uncertainty propagation through a 3-compartment rapamycin model: Blood, Brain (BBB-limited), Peripheral (fast-eq. tissues).
comments: Rapamycin (Sirolimus) Epistemic PBPK Test Suite
Validates GUM-based uncertainty propagation through a 3-compartment
rapamycin model: Blood, Brain (BBB-limited), Peripheral (fast-eq. tissues).
Model choice: Distribution-capped 3-compartment (NOT full 14-compartment).
- Brain compartment: kp_brain=0.08 (P-gp efflux at BBB) — PRESERVED accurately
- Peripheral: v_periph=50L, kp_periph=0.5 → t1/2 ~ 21h (tractable for 48h)
- Adipose deep sequestration (kp_adipose~15) excluded by design
(would require multi-week simulation for CL to be observable in AUC)
Epistemic parameters:
- cl_hepatic: 12.4 L/h, Var=54.76 (CV=60%, CYP3A4 polymorphism, Ferron 1997)
- kp_brain: 0.08, Var=0.000625 (SD=0.025, P-gp efflux, Lampen 1998)
- fu_plasma: 0.08, Var=0.0004 (SD=0.02, 92% bound, Schreiber 1991)
GUM step sizes: h = max(1e-6 * |mean|, 1e-2 * SD)  [GPT review correction]
Confidence: evidence-quality score [0,1], NOT Beta distribution
(Beta appropriate only for [0,1]-bounded quantities; CL is unbounded)
6 tests:
1. Simulation completes successfully
2. Brain/plasma ratio < 0.15 (P-gp efflux verified)
3. CV(AUC_0_48) > 30% (CYP3A4 inter-individual variability)
4. All epistemic variances > 0
5. AUC(CL/2) > AUC(CL_ref) — causal monotonicity check
6. CL dominates AUC uncertainty: s_cl > 0.5

9.  Parallel transport preserves norm in Euclidean space

11.  Metric determinant of sphere: det(g) = sin^2(theta) at theta=pi/4
12.  Raise and lower index roundtrip

instruction: Write a Sounio compile-fail example named `potential_outcome_both_observed`. potential outcome linear violation — cannot observe both Y(0) and Y(1) for same unit. It should fail to compile. The compiler output should include: E073.
description: potential outcome linear violation — cannot observe both Y(0) and Y(1) for same unit
comments: The Fundamental Problem of Causal Inference (Holland 1986):
For any unit i, only ONE of {Y_i(0), Y_i(1)} can ever be observed.
Y_i(0) = outcome under control; Y_i(1) = outcome under treatment.
Sounio enforces this via linear types: PotentialOutcome<T> is consumed on observation.
Attempting to use BOTH Y(0) and Y(1) for the same unit violates the linear type constraint (E073).
This tests the PO track (Sprint 20): TyPotentialOutcome<T> as a linearly-consumed type.
The individual treatment effect ITE = Y(1) - Y(0) is unobservable for any single unit;
only the Average Treatment Effect ATE = E[Y(1) - Y(0)] can be estimated from a population.
Reference: Holland 1986, Rubin 1974, Imbens & Rubin 2015 (Causal Inference for Statistics).

description: potential outcome linear violation — cannot observe both Y(0) and Y(1) for same unit
